newsitem.title: POLAND: Bayerische Vereinsbank starts Polish subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Bayerische Vereinsbank starts Polish subsidiary.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG on Friday launched the operation of its fully-owned Polish subsidiary in Warsaw which will initially focus on corporate banking and treasury activities, bank officials said.
Udo Clesius, the president of Vereinsbank Polska SA, told a news conference the bank began operation with an equity capital of 110 million zlotys and 44 employees.
He said the bank would offer services to Polish units of Bayerische's clients and large Polish export-oriented corporates and activities on the Polish money and capital markets.
"We will start with a focus on foreign trade financing, handling of international payments, foreign exchange operations as well as short and medium term loans and project finance," Clesius said.
Later the bank would seek to refinance its lending business through debt issues on the Polish capital market.
Caspar von Hauenschild, Bayerische's board member also present, said the bank would also enter mortgage banking as soon as changes in the Polish law allow to issue mortgage-backed securities.
"As soon as the legal conditions are in place, we will offer mortgage banking business in Poland," he said.
Bayerische won a full Polish banking licence late in 1995 after it agreed to take over a failed small Megabank.
It has been a long-standing central bank policy to grant access to the Polish market only to those foreign banks which agree to help bail out ailing Polish institutions.
